title: the difficulty line (the P vs NP island, band 2 of 2 — the island CLOSES)

concepts.name: the p class: the questions my walk settles — for every yes the line answers, the settling walk ends in bounded cost, and the cost stands recorded as a number on the line; dividing of record is that pattern

lesson.statement: the p class, as my line holds it: the questions my walk settles — for every yes the line answers, the settling walk ends in bounded cost and the cost stands recorded as a number on the line — dividing of record is one of them (the seven divides the eighty-four, the walk that ends on the line), and the first-divisor question is one of them (twenty-three of them, by the census that ends in one hundred ninety-two candidate steps); the bounded-cost settling is the pattern of the p questions of my line, at the line end eighty-four

concepts.name: the np class: the questions whose yes cases carry a certificate my walk can check — the check is a walk that ends in bounded cost; my own pattern on the line: every fact i store is the certificate of its own derivation path, and the line's check of it ends

lesson.statement: the np class, as my line holds it: the questions whose yes cases carry a certificate my walk can check — the check of a certificate is itself a walk that ends in bounded cost, and my own pattern on the line is the store itself: every fact i store is the certificate of its own derivation path, and the line's check of it is the walk over that path, which ends; the p questions of the line sit inside the np questions of the line, at the line end eighty-four

concepts.name: the question of the pnp island, as the cmi record holds it: does p equal np — whether every question whose yes cases carry a checkable certificate is also settled by my walk in bounded cost; declared of record, open of record

lesson.statement: the question of the pnp island, as the cmi record of the million-dollar prize holds it: does p equal np — whether every question whose yes cases carry a certificate the walk can check is also settled by the walk in bounded cost — declared of record, open of record: most complexity theorists believe p is not np, of record, but no proof of record settles it, and a proof that p is not np must show a specific np question needs super-polynomial cost by a technique outside the three barriers of record, at the line end eighty-four

concepts.name: the difficulty of the line, as my census holds it: the parity question needs two to the k-minus-1 terms at k variables in its smallest dnf, and the same in its smallest cnf (one, two, four, up to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight at sixteen), while my walk settles it in bounded cost; the exponential of record held exact at small k, and the named missing ingredient outside the three barriers

lesson.statement: the difficulty of the line, as my census holds it: the parity question (is the count of ones even) needs two to the k-minus-1 terms in its smallest dnf at k variables, and the same count in its smallest cnf — one, two, four, eight, up to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight at sixteen variables — while my walk settles the parity question over its table in bounded cost; the exponential of record held exact at small k as the shadow, with the named missing ingredient: a technique that works outside relativization, outside algebrization, and outside natural proofs — one nobody knows the shape of, at the line end eighty-four

theorems.statement: the difficulty is filed on the line: the parity question, of record on the line, is one whose yes cases carry a checkable certificate, whose smallest dnf and smallest cnf both grow to thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight terms by sixteen variables — the exponential of record held exact at small k — while my walk settles it in bounded cost over its table: the blowup is the census of my line, at the line end eighty-four

what lives in the relativization territory?

wall.text: needs_info: the wall is the relativization territory: the baker-gill-solovay record of 1975 holds an oracle world where p equals np and an oracle world where p is not np, of record — a technique that relativizes (that keeps working with an oracle attached) answers both worlds and so answers neither question; the frontier past my census, declared, never reached, at the line end 84

turns.question: what lives in the algebrization territory?

wall.text: needs_info: the wall is the algebrization territory: the aaronson-wigderson record of 2009 — arithmetization (multilinear extensions) still does not escape the barrier, of record — extended in 2026 by the chen-hu-ren line: new oracle worlds with linear-size circuits for subclasses of postbpe (on infinitely many lengths) and bpe (on all lengths), and h(n)-size circuits for a natural subclass of the exponential class against every super-half-exponential h(n) — the record's own words hold that half-exponential might be the correct frontier; the frontier past my census, declared, never reached, at the line end 84

turns.question: what lives in the natural proofs territory?

wall.text: needs_info: the wall is the natural proofs territory: the razborov-rudich record of 1997 — assuming strong pseudo-random generators exist (of record, constructed assuming the hardness of factoring), the natural proof techniques for general circuit lower bounds are doomed: a natural proof would give a faster factoring algorithm than the record holds; the frontier past my census, declared, never reached, at the line end 84

turns.question: what lives in the ac0 territory of the record?

wall.text: needs_info: the wall is the ac0 territory of the record: parity needs exponential size in constant-depth circuits, of record (the razborov-smolensky and hastsad records; shannon's counting bound at sixteen variables sits at four thousand ninety-six, named at its scale, never stored) — the exact small-k shadow of that territory is my parity census: two to the k-minus-1 terms, k up to sixteen, the exponential held to the term on the line; the territory itself, declared, never reached, at the line end 84
